deck.title: DAMA-DMBOK Chapter 1 — Data Management Study Summary

slides.title: Example: The Data–Information Cycle
slides.intro: The same content alternates between being 'data' and 'information' depending on the role it plays and the purpose it serves.

steps.label: Information
steps.detail: Sales report for last quarter — a meaningful output presented to stakeholders

steps.label: Data
steps.detail: Underlying records from the data warehouse — the raw input that generates the report

steps.label: Data (re-used)
steps.detail: Those same quarterly results, now treated as input data for the next calculation

steps.label: Information
steps.detail: Quarter-over-quarter performance measures — new information derived from the prior results

slides.title: Data as an Organizational Asset
slides.label: Core Definition
slides.definition: An asset is an economic resource, that can be owned or controlled, and that holds or produces value. Assets can be converted to money.
notes: Data is widely recognised as an enterprise asset, though understanding what it means to manage it as one is still evolving
Goodwill analogy: in the early 1990s, 'value of goodwill' on the P&L was questioned — now it is standard. Monetisation of data is following the same trajectory
Data-driven organisations replace gut-feeling decisions with event triggers and analytics to gain actionable insight
Effective management of data as an asset requires a partnership of business leadership and technical expertise

children.label: DM is a Business Requirement
children: Metadata is required to manage data
Planning is required to manage data
DM requirements must drive IT decisions

children.label: DM is Lifecycle Management
children: Data has a lifecycle to manage
Risk management is part of DM

columns.heading: Data has Unique Properties
bullets: Unlike financial or physical assets, data is not consumed when it is used
The same data can be used by multiple people simultaneously
Data does not wear out, though its value may change with age
Many uses of data beget more data — volumes and relationships grow continuously

columns.heading: Metadata is Essential
bullets: Because data cannot be held or touched, understanding it requires definition and knowledge in the form of Metadata
Metadata originates from architecture, modeling, stewardship, governance, Data Quality management, systems development, IT operations, and analytics
Managing data requires Metadata about that data

columns.heading: Data is Lifecycle Management
bullets: Data has a lifecycle; managing data means managing that lifecycle
Because data begets more data, the data lifecycle can be very complex
Different types of data have different lifecycle characteristics and therefore different management requirements

summary: 2.5.13 — Effective data management requires leadership and commitment
